announcements.name: Claude model family available in Microsoft Foundry
announcements.shortDescription: Claude Opus, Claude Sonnet, and Claude Haiku are deployable in Foundry with shared safety, prompting strategies, API patterns, and identical environment across the three models.
announcements.longDescription: The Claude model family is available in Microsoft Foundry, including Claude Opus, Claude Sonnet [inferred] (transcribed as 'Claude Summit'), and Claude Haiku, positioned among the best models for coding and agentic workflows. Because they are a family, you get the same safety, prompting strategies, environment, and API calls across all three models, allowing you to switch between them depending on the use case. Claude Opus is described as the most intelligent model for genuinely hard problems such as complex reasoning, deep coding across large or unfamiliar code bases, and long-horizon agentic tasks, with the ability to stay coherent over extended runs. Sonnet is described as a strong default.

announcements.name: Claude Agent SDK as a supported harness
announcements.shortDescription: The same agent loop, tools, and context management behind Claude Code is programmable in Python and TypeScript and can run inside Foundry.
announcements.longDescription: The Claude Agent SDK is the harness behind Claude Code — the same agent loop, tools, and context management that power the product used by millions of developers daily — and it is programmable in both Python and TypeScript. The loop is to gather context, take action, verify the work, and repeat until the task is done. Out of the box it provides code execution, a file system, web search, a to-do list, and MCP, plus support for your own custom tools. It also includes infrastructure around the loop, including context management, sessions and memory, permissions, and lifecycle hooks.

announcements.name: Foundry hosted agents
announcements.shortDescription: Custom-code agents (built with the Claude Agent SDK, GitHub Copilot SDK, LangChain, or LangGraph) can be moved from a local machine into an automatically secured cloud sandbox in Foundry Agent Service.
announcements.longDescription: Foundry hosted agents are agents you build with custom code in any framework you want — including the GitHub Copilot SDK, LangChain, LangGraph, or the Claude Agent SDK — and run within Microsoft Foundry inside a hosted container sandbox. You start by building and testing the agent on your local machine, then move the application up into the cloud sandbox hosted in Foundry Agent Service. The sandbox is automatically secured and set up with the authentication needed to access Foundry resources, such as calling Claude models in Microsoft Foundry. It also facilitates the authentication needed to securely connect to tools and MCPs that host your enterprise data.

announcements.name: Claude availability through GitHub Copilot
announcements.shortDescription: Claude is reachable through GitHub Copilot and Azure AI Foundry, working with existing M365 identity and data without changing developer environments.
announcements.longDescription: Claude is natively integrated with the Microsoft stack: it is available in Azure AI Foundry, works with the identity and data already managed in M365, and is available through GitHub Copilot. As a result, developers don't need to change their environment, and security and platform teams don't take on a new vendor surface to review. On Azure it also sits inside existing governance — data handling, access controls, content filtering, audit, and compliance — so capability isn't traded for control.

announcements.name: Built-in evaluation and observability
announcements.shortDescription: Foundry records agent sessions, traces, tool calls, and offers evaluators (groundedness, coherence, relevance, task adherence, code vulnerability) plus custom evaluators, accessible via UI and programmatically.
announcements.longDescription: Microsoft Foundry provides built-in observability for hosted agents, showing the agent in the project and all of the sessions that have run for it. Opening a session reveals the steps taken and produced artifacts, such as a weekly forecast chart and an executive summary in markdown, which are available in Foundry and can be accessed programmatically. You can also view the trace of the agent's activity, including all the turns and tool calls the Claude Agent SDK made while running the workflow. In the demo, the presenter used Claude Code to wire up trace recording for the Foundry hosted agent by having it look up the documentation, then viewed and played back the agent's actions and step metadata in Foundry.
